finding.shortLabel: 'John Cheny' of the 1661 Braintree record = John Gurney
finding.statement: The 'John Cheny' of the 1661 Braintree marriage and wife-death lines is John Gurney. The fair-copy manuscript reads 'John Girny, Senior' in ink, with 'Cheny' only a later pencil margin annotation that the 1886 print mistook for text; Pope 1900 independently ruled the printed Cheny a typographical error; no John Cheney family is otherwise attested at Braintree in 1661; and the surrounding facts fit Gurney — Mary Gurney's death three weeks earlier, the officiant Peter Brackett (a documented Gurney associate), and John Gurney's 1663 Braintree probate. Confidence is roughly 85-90%, the residual being the ambiguous deaths-page letterform.

finding.statement: The Braintree town-record manuscript, read at image level, shows the fair-copy marriages register (p. 174) ink main text as 'John Girny, Senior (and) Grizell ——X——, by Peter Brackett, 9mo 12, 1661' — the groom 'Girny,' an attested Gurney variant, carrying the copyist's uncertain-reading underline; the bride's surname left blank. 'Cheny / Kidbee' appears only in a later pencil hand in the left margin. The 17th-century original deaths page reads '[?]eny the wiffe of John [?]eny dyed the 7th month 20, 1661,' the initial letterform ambiguous between secretary-hand Ch and G.

finding.shortLabel: 1886 Braintree print: 'John Cheny' marriage & wife-death lines, 1661

sources.excerpt: John Cheny Senior and Grizell Kidbee ... Cheny the wife of John Cheny

finding.statement: The 1886 printed Braintree town record (Bates ed.) enters John Gurney's second marriage and his first wife's death under a Cheny surname: p. 717, 'John Cheny Senior and Grizell Kidbee,' 9th month 12, 1661 (12 November 1661); and p. 638, 'Cheny the wife of John Cheny,' 7th month 20, 1661 (20 September 1661). Both dates match the Gurney chronology but the printed surname is Cheny, not Gurney.

outgoing.explanation: Pope's independent 1900 records-based ruling that the printed 'John Cheny' is a typographical error corroborates the Gurney reading.

finding.shortLabel: Pope 1900: printed Braintree 'John Cheny' a typographical error for John Gurney

sources.excerpt: He is called John Cheny, Sen., in the printed records of Braintree, by a typographical error.
sources.locator: GURNET/GORNET entry, print p. ~204 (Internet Archive pioneersofmassac00pope)

finding.statement: Charles Henry Pope, The Pioneers of Massachusetts (1900), entering John Gurney of Braintree under the head-form 'GURNET, GORNET,' states that 'he is called John Cheny, Sen., in the printed records of Braintree, by a typographical error,' and reads both the 20 (7) 1661 wife-death line and the 12 (9) 1661 marriage to 'Grizzell, widow of Henry Kibbee' as the Gurney family — an independent, records-based 1900 ruling that the printed Cheny is an error for Gurney.
